label: copy-phase input s/w near the end of long sequences (very sparse subset)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is s or w (these two account for >99% of activation mass). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on first occurrences. Activity sits in the last ~3 copy steps (to_go<=2 holds 96% of mass, to_go=0 holds 55%) at late absolute steps (t>=11, rate rising to t=17), plus the last step of L=3 sequences; L=4 and 5 never fire. The predicate captures ~94% of activations and 96% of mass but has only ~3% precision: the neuron fires on just a small, unexplained subset of these s/w steps. Preceding inputs e or x raise the rate (precision ~14%) but are not a clean rule. Magnitude is tiny (max 0.008) and the strongest examples are late-step w or s, often right after e or x.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+5.97), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+5.71), L=3 & t=5 (+4.68), prev_tok=e (+2.70), to_go=0 (+2.64), phase=2 & out_tok=x (+2.12). Lower it: out_tok=2 (-1.77), orig8=- (-1.67), to_go=3 (-1.59), prev_tok=n (-1.32).
